zh.title: 達美航空擬以空中巴士A330neo替代767 著重高階配置
zh.summary: 達美航空將以A330neo取代老化767機隊；配備高階客艙並鎖定跨大西洋航線
body: 根據網路媒體 Simple Flying 報導，達美航空（Delta Air Lines）正計劃以配備更多高階艙等的空中巴士（Airbus）A330-900neo 客機，來汰換旗下老化的 767-300ER 寬體客機機隊。達美航空此次並非僅是單純增加座位總數，而是著重於升級客艙產品品質。
根據達美航空先前的機隊規劃資料，這批全新的空中巴士 A330-900neo 客機將會配備多達 56 個 Delta One 套房艙。達美航空引進此種以高階客艙為主的配置，主要是為了鎖定其核心的跨大西洋航線。

en.title: Delta Air Lines to Replace Aging 767s With Premium-Heavy Airbus A330neos
en.summary: Delta Air Lines will replace aging 767s with premium Airbus A330neos on major transatlantic routes.
body: According to a report by Simple Flying, Delta Air Lines is planning to replace its aging fleet of 767-300ER aircraft with a more premium-heavy Airbus A330-900neo product. Instead of focusing on increasing the overall passenger seat count, the carrier is aiming to deliver a more premium travel experience.

The carrier's strategy includes deploying these configured Airbus A330-900neo aircraft to target its top transatlantic routes. Based on previous corporate fleet details, Delta's new Airbus A330-900neo cabin layout will feature a total of 56 Delta One suites to cater to high-end transatlantic demand.

zh.title: 英國Strasser計劃鼓勵飛行員及早轉降
zh.summary: 英國通用航空安全倡議；參與機場免除緊急或非預期轉降的降落費
body: 《Aerospace Global News》報導，Strasser計劃是英國一項通用航空安全倡議，旨在去除飛行員因顧慮降落費過高而延誤進行預防性降落的力量。
根據報導，參與計劃的英國機場同意，當通用航空飛機確屬緊急情況或非預期性的預防性轉降時，免除降落費用。
該計劃源自1997年民航局（CAA）的檢討（CAP 667），內容為「審查1985至1994年通用航空致命意外」。該報告建議機場所有者採取緊急和轉降降落免費的政策。
此建議由航空倡議人士暨AOPA英國代表Charles Strasser接手，他遊說個別機場營運者參與，使計劃發展為參與機場與通用航空社群之間的自願協議。
AOPA強調，濫用此計劃可能削弱參與機場的信譽並威脅計劃宗旨。

en.title: UK's Strasser Scheme encourages precautionary landings by waiving fees
en.summary: UK GA safety initiative; participating airfields waive landing charges for genuine emergency or unforeseen precautionary diversions
body: The Strasser Scheme is a British general aviation safety initiative designed to remove the disincentive of landing fees when pilots need to make a precautionary landing, according to Aerospace Global News.
Under the scheme, participating UK aerodromes agree to waive landing charges when a general-aviation aircraft makes a genuine emergency or unforeseen precautionary diversion.

The scheme's origins trace to a 1997 Civil Aviation Authority review (CAP 667), titled 'Review of General Aviation Fatal Accidents 1985 to 1994', which recommended that aerodrome owners adopt a policy of making emergency and diversionary landings free of charge for general aviation aircraft.

The recommendation was taken up by Charles Strasser, an aviation campaigner and AOPA UK representative, who persuaded individual aerodrome operators to participate, making the scheme a voluntary agreement rather than a regulatory rule.
AOPA has emphasised that abuse could undermine the confidence of participating airfields and threaten the initiative's purpose.
